text.p: Shares in National Westminster Bank Plc led a rebound in the bank sector on Friday after a strong performance in U.S. banks on Thursday, dealers said.
They said the bounce in U.S. bank shares, which rose even as the Dow lost almost 40 points, sparked bargain-hunting in the UK sector.
By 1026 GMT, NatWest shares were up 18-1/2p to 693-1/2, having tumbled 159-1/2, or 19 percent, from their February 17 closing peak at 834-1/2p.
"This is just an overdue bounce," said one London dealer.

Elsewhere, shares in Abbey National Plc added 12-1/2p to 740-1/2, while Lloyds TSB Group shares climbed 7-1/2p to 498. Shares in Barclays Plc rose 9p to 1021-1/2, and shares in HSBC Holdings firmed 23p to 1447-1/2.

Dealers said investors were inspired by the strength in most major U.S. bank shares, like Chase Manhattan Corp, which rose $1-1/8 to $93-1/2, and Citicorp, which climbed $1-5/8 to 111-5/8, in a declining market.
